verdict.rationale: First-party docs describe automatic extraction of memories from raw content and background-maintained user profiles that update as users interact (docs-1, docs-15, docs-33, docs-40, docs-41, docs-55), which directly matches the story of self-deciding salience and background consolidation. However, Supermemory's own comparison doc flags a real limitation — it has 'no temporal truth,' so conflicting facts ('loved Adidas' then 'switched to Puma') both remain equally relevant rather than being resolved/consolidated, undercutting the 'consolidating' half of the story, and there's no independent hands-on evidence of extraction quality. missing for 10: independent/hands-on verification that extraction and consolidation actually resolve conflicting or redundant facts well, and resolution of the documented temporal-truth gap.
